points.text: Differentiation from LGA/LES thin; no LGA-style baseline or no-descriptor ablation.
Claim that LQD can represent any QD algorithm not true of parameterization.
Discovery of novel QD algorithms not demonstrated; no rule extracted.
Emitter-based QD baselines missing.
Earlier meta-evolution of QD algorithms not discussed.
Equivariance and invariance used interchangeably.
Abstract/introduction claims of superiority and state-of-the-art broader than results.
Key quantities and normalizations hard to interpret; no absolute-number table.
Manuscript in ACM format with placeholder dates.
QD claim not shown: F+N below DNS; robots use only LQD(F).
Huge meta-training search versus untuned baselines; unfair comparison.
Validation tasks, meta-training run count and selection protocol undefined.
Diversity-as-instrumental-goal not tested against softer selection or fitness sharing.
Random-descriptor control uses out-of-range inputs; significance untested.
Generalization shown on training functions against ME only.
Robot task count inconsistent.
Normalization to Random undefined for non-positive values.
Aggregation behind p < 0.005 not described.
Baselines untuned and hyperparameters unspecified while LQD had enormous tuning budget.
Generalization sweep uses training functions, one baseline, one variant.
Metrics do not test QD: no archive QD score or coverage; non-standard QD score.
Statistics cover inference seeds only; meta-training seeds, selection, validation set unstated.
Aggregation behind Figure 1 p-value not described.
Johnson-Lindenstrauss justification inapplicable; D unstated; descriptors only linear projections.
Task count inconsistency, placeholder dates, typo.
Instrumental-diversity story needs fitness-sharing or crowding control.
Descriptor ablation feeds unseen noise; use descriptor shuffling.
Runtime and meta-training cost not reported; no wall-clock comparison.
Learned descriptors (AURORA-style) and other settings unexplored.
No limitations or societal-impact paragraph.
Some methods and results insufficiently clear.
A few claims unsupported.
Some figures have issues.
Relevant variants and ablations missing.
No comparison with descriptor-learning approaches like AURORA.
Recent MetaBBO and QD related work largely neglected.
Learning selection via transformer not novel versus Lange et al., GLHF.
Controlling only selection is too inflexible to discover new algorithms.
Claim that fitness-only LQD maintains diversity questionable; why worse than QD variant.
No comparison with existing MetaBBO approaches.
Unclear why robot control needs QD.
Descriptor dimension D not given; distance-preservation claim unproven.
Reproduction size B undefined.
8-H100 meta-training too costly for results merely competitive with GA/ME.
Narrow GA-only view of QD; baselines omit PGA-ME, PPGA, BOP-Elites, CMA-MAE.
No discussion of integrating LQD with CMA-MAE; CMA-MAE may dominate.
Table 4 lacks p-values or variance.
No scalability analysis over problem dimension across methods.
Limited ablation; transformer architecture and size impact unexplored.
No comparison with CMA-ES.

P.summary: Delta from LGA/LES unclear; no LGA-style baseline.
Related work on meta-evolving QD missing.
Metrics and normalizations hard to interpret.
Baselines untuned versus massive LQD meta-training.
Validation set and meta-training seeds undefined.
Instrumental diversity claim lacks fitness-sharing control.
Generalization tested on training functions vs ME only.

Q.summary: Novelty vs Lange et al. and GLHF.
Motivation for QD in robot control.
